disclaimer.title: Important notice: read before using wIA
disclaimer.html:
wIA is an educational and experimental project with no commercial purpose. It is not a product or a professional service: it is provided “as is”, without warranties of any kind and free of charge.

How wIA is used is entirely the user’s responsibility: what they write, the data and documents they load, the engines and providers they connect, the keys they enter and what they do with the answers. AI models can be wrong or make things up and do not replace professional judgement or advice (legal, medical, financial or otherwise).

wIA uses no servers of its own to process or store your data: everything runs and is kept in the user’s browser memory (conversations, documents, settings and keys). Only the external AI engines the user connects receive what is sent to them.

Do not enter third parties’ personal data, professional secrets or any information you have no right to process or to send to an external provider.

The API keys, accounts and third-party services they connect are theirs, as are the costs and conditions each provider applies. The use of wIA, and of everything it generates or processes, is the user’s sole responsibility.

4. Disclaimer of liability

wIA is provided “as is” and “as available”. The owner and the author do not guarantee that it is accurate, complete, uninterrupted or fit for a particular purpose, and are not liable for:

  • the answers of AI models, which may be wrong, incomplete, biased or invented, or for decisions taken on the basis of them;
  • the operation, availability, prices or data handling of the third-party providers the user connects;
  • data loss: conversations are stored only in the browser and can be lost when site data is cleared or the device changes; make backups;
  • damage arising from misuse, from data entered without a legal basis or from the user’s chosen configuration.

5. Intellectual property

wIA’s source code is distributed under the MIT license. Third-party models, trademarks, names and services mentioned belong to their respective owners and are cited for identification purposes only. Users are responsible for ensuring that what they load and what they obtain from the models respects third-party rights.

7. Governing law and jurisdiction

These terms are governed by Spanish law. For any dispute, the parties submit to the courts that correspond under the applicable rules, including consumer-protection rules where relevant.

sections.title: Privacy policy
sections.html:
1. Summary

  • wIA has no user accounts and no database of its own. Your conversations, documents and settings are stored in your browser; the owner does not receive them.
  • There is no analytics, advertising or tracking.
  • What you write does leave your device when you choose a cloud engine: it goes straight to the provider you configured (see section 4). With a local or in-browser engine, it does not.
  • You have tools to reduce this: local 🕶️ anonymization, Incognito mode, PIN lock and encrypted keys.

2. Data controller

Tligent, S.L., tax ID B05381082, registered at San Vicenç Ferrer 24, bajos, 08940 Cornellà de Llobregat (Barcelona). Contact: info@tligent.com. The owner only processes the technical access data of the site (section 3). The content the user handles with wIA is decided and controlled by the user, who is responsible for its legal basis; if used personally, it is a purely personal or household activity (art. 2.2.c GDPR).

3. What data is processed, where and why

DataWherePurposeLegal basis (GDPR)Retention

4. Recipients and third-party services

The owner does not disclose data to third parties. But wIA is a client that talks to the services you connect, and those services receive what you send them:

  • Cloud AI providers (for example Groq, OpenRouter, Google Gemini, Anthropic, OpenAI, Mistral, Cerebras, NVIDIA or Ollama Cloud): they receive your messages, the documents and excerpts you attach or retrieve and the images you send, together with your API key. They process this under their own privacy policy and terms, and some may use it to improve their models unless you opt out in your account.
  • Local engines (Ollama, LM Studio, LocalAI, local gateways such as FreeLLMAPI): they run on your device or network; wIA only sends them the request. Some gateways forward to cloud providers in turn.
  • In-browser models (WebGPU): inference happens on your device. To work, models are downloaded from Hugging Face and, if not in the local copy, the inference runtime from jsDelivr (CDN); those services see your IP and what is downloaded.
  • Web search: if you enable tools and the model decides to search, the query is sent to DuckDuckGo or Wikipedia.
  • Voice dictation: uses the browser’s own speech recognition; depending on the browser, audio may be sent to its vendor’s servers.
  • Optional CORS proxy (Node server bundled with wIA): forwards the request to the provider without storing it; it only exists if you run it or the deployment includes it.
  • OpenRouter sign-in (optional, OAuth PKCE): your password never goes through wIA; only an API key for your account is received.
  • Hosting (Vercel and/or the owner’s own server): serves the application files and may log technical access data.

Some of these providers are outside the European Economic Area; those transfers are governed by the safeguards each provider offers (adequacy decisions, standard contractual clauses…). The user chooses which provider receives their data.

5. Local anonymization

The 🕶️ mode replaces sensitive data (national IDs, e-mails, phone numbers, IBANs, names, etc.) with placeholders before the message is sent; the map to reverse them stays encrypted in your browser and the answer is restored only on screen. It is an aid, not a guarantee: it may miss some data, does not act on images or file names, and the result should be reviewed before sending.

6. Your rights

For the data the owner processes, you may exercise your rights of access, rectification, erasure, objection, restriction and portability by writing to info@tligent.com. The data wIA keeps in your browser is under your direct control (you can delete it from Settings or from the browser’s settings). To exercise your rights against an AI provider, contact it directly. If you consider your request has not been handled properly, you may complain to the Spanish Data Protection Agency (www.aepd.es).

7. Security

  • API keys are stored encrypted (AES-GCM) with a non-exportable browser key.
  • Backups can be password-protected (PBKDF2-SHA256 + AES-GCM).
  • The PIN lock and Incognito mode reduce exposure on shared devices, but they do not replace device encryption or the operating system’s access control: anyone with access to your browser profile can reach its data.
  • The application enforces a strict Content Security Policy (CSP) and loads its resources from the site itself, except for the services listed above.

8. Minors

wIA is not aimed at children under 14. If you are a minor, use it only under the supervision of a parent or guardian.

9. Changes

This policy may be updated when the application changes. The date of the latest review is shown at the end.

sections.title: Cookies and storage
sections.html:
A cookie is a small file a site saves in your browser. wIA sets no cookies of its own; it uses the browser’s local storage (localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB and the service worker cache), which works in a similar way.

1. What we use

Only technical items or personalisation you choose, exempt from consent under article 22.2 of the LSSI-CE. We use no analytics, advertising or tracking.

NameTypePurposeDuration

Model cacheCache StorageDownloaded WebGPU model weights, to avoid downloading againUntil you remove them
antigravity_chats, antigravity_projectslocalStorage (legacy)Data from old versions, migrated and removedUntil migrated

If you use a third-party service (for example OpenRouter’s sign-in or a provider’s website), that site may set its own cookies on its domain, under its own policies.

2. How to manage it

You can view and delete all of this from your browser’s privacy settings (“site data”). If you clear storage you will lose your conversations, settings and saved keys: make a backup first (Settings → Data). With Incognito mode on, conversations are not saved in the browser.

3. Changes

If something requiring consent were ever added, it would be requested before installing it and this page would be updated.

sections.title: Regulatory compliance
sections.html:
1. Nature of the service

wIA is an educational and experimental project with no commercial purpose. It provides no professional services, does not hold the user’s data (it stays in their browser) and takes no actions on its own beyond those the user orders.

2. Not professional advice

Nothing the models generate constitutes legal, medical, health, financial, tax or any other advice, nor does it replace the opinion of a qualified professional. Models labelled “medical” or similar are indicative and are not medical devices. Before acting on an answer, check it against reliable sources.

3. Use of artificial intelligence and transparency

Answers are generated by third-party or local artificial-intelligence models, not by a person, and may contain errors, bias or invented content. They are identified as such in the application, in line with the transparency obligations of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on artificial intelligence. In addition, 100% of the content, text and code of this page were created using artificial-intelligence tools.

4. The user’s responsibility as a data handler

If you use wIA in a professional context or with other people’s data, you are the one responsible for the legal basis of the processing, for informing data subjects, for signing the processing agreements with the relevant providers, for international transfers and for not sending special categories of data (health, beliefs, etc.) without a legal basis and adequate safeguards. Consider using a local engine or 🕶️ anonymization in those cases.

5. Data protection and cookies

Personal data processing follows Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) and Spanish Organic Law 3/2018 (LOPDGDD). Details in the privacy policy and the cookies and storage page.

6. Reference rules

  • Law 34/2002 on information society services and e-commerce (LSSI-CE).
  • Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) and Organic Law 3/2018 (LOPDGDD).
  • Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on artificial intelligence.
  • Royal Legislative Decree 1/1996 on intellectual property, and the code’s MIT license.

7. Contact and incidents

For questions, errors or security incidents, write to info@tligent.com.
